name: W_boson

phase_0.boundary_condition: Electroweak symmetry breaking scale (v ≈ 246 GeV) — the Higgs mechanism closes the system by giving mass to the W boson and defining the finite range of weak interactions

⊢.justification: Unbroken SU(2)×U(1) gauge symmetry with massless gauge fields; no W boson exists as a distinct particle before symmetry breaking

⊣.justification: Higgs field acquires VEV, W boson gains mass (80.38 GeV), weak force becomes short-range — the closed boundary containing all weak interaction physics

≻.justification: Forward morphism: d → u + W⁻ or e⁻ → νₑ + W⁻ — fermion flavor changes upward in weak isospin, mediated by W⁺ propagation

≺.justification: Reverse morphism: u → d + W⁺ or νₑ → e⁻ + W⁺ — fermion flavor changes downward, the contravariant descent transformation

⋈.chosen_element: Sequential weak vertices in Feynman diagram
⋈.justification: Composition of multiple W exchanges (e.g., muon decay: μ⁻ → νₘ + W⁻, then W⁻ → e⁻ + ν̄ₑ) — chaining morphisms along fermion lines

⊙.justification: Identity: the W field recognizes itself in the gauge kinetic term (W⁺ᵘW⁻ᵤ) and triple gauge vertex (W⁺W⁻γ/Z) — self-reference of the gauge field

∈.justification: One W vertex splits into multiple possible fermion-antifermion pairs: (u,d̄), (c,s̄), (e⁻,ν̄ₑ), (μ⁻,ν̄ₘ), (τ⁻,ν̄ₜ) — the co-multiplication δ opening all weak isospin doublet channels

∋.justification: Rejoin: the μ multiplication fuses all flavor amplitudes into the total weak current — interference between generations (CKM mixing) reconstitutes the single interaction vertex

⊤.justification: Constructive truth: transitions with large CKM elements (e.g., u↔d, c↔s, e↔νₑ) — affirmative arm where weak interaction proceeds with high probability

⊥.justification: Constructive falsity: transitions with small CKM elements (e.g., u↔b, c↔d) — negative arm where amplitude is constructively refuted by unitarity constraints

⊞.justification: Paradice: both amplitudes held simultaneously — e.g., K⁰-K̄⁰ mixing where W box diagrams carry both ΔS=1 and ΔS=-1 phases, B state as live contradiction in the kaon system

⊡.justification: ROM fixation: a specific weak decay (e.g., μ⁻ → e⁻ + ν̄ₑ + νₘ) recorded in a particle detector — irreversible, append-only measurement that cannot be undone

phase_2.split_input: Incoming fermion line (e.g., muon) at weak vertex
phase_2.fuse_result: Total weak current with CKM interference — conflicting arms (favored vs suppressed) rejoin to B (both) when CP violation makes them simultaneously contributory
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: Unbroken electroweak vacuum — no massive W, no flavor-changing weak force, fermions massless
phase_3.true_description: Observed weak decay with CKM-favored transition — e.g., muon decay, nuclear beta decay
phase_3.false_description: Forbidden or heavily suppressed transition — e.g., flavor-changing neutral current, ΔS=2 without CKM phase
phase_3.both_description: CP-violating interference — e.g., K⁰-K̄⁰ oscillation where both straminent and antistrangeness amplitudes coexist in the mass eigenstates

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑡: The W boson mediates weak interactions between fermions across a connected graph of flavor-changing vertices, forming a hub-spoke pattern where the boson couples to particle-antiparticle pairs in a network of gauge interactions.
⊢=𐑼: The W boson operates as a point-like gauge interaction vertex in the Standard Model Lagrangian, coupling locally to fermion fields at a single spacetime point.
⊞=𐑳: The W boson couples asymmetrically to fermion pairs with different flavors and charges (e.g., up-type quark to down-type quark, or charged lepton to neutrino), creating distinct particle-antiparticle vertex counts on each side of the interaction.
⊡=𐑴: The W boson's role as a gauge boson is protected by the electroweak SU(2)×U(1) gauge symmetry, requiring a topological phase transition (spontaneous symmetry breaking) to remove its mediating function, analogous to crossing a Z2 boundary.
⊙=𐑢: The W boson operates in the normal electroweak regime at energies far below the Planck scale, exhibiting massive propagator behavior with finite correlation lengths and no scale-free critical fluctuations.
⊥=𐑖: The W boson couples exclusively to left-handed fermions and right-handed antifermions, enforcing a structurally persistent chiral asymmetry through the V−A structure of the weak interaction that cannot be thermally flipped.
≻=𐑽: The W boson acts as a gauge force mediator that enables flavor-changing transitions by lowering the energy barrier for weak decays without being consumed, functioning as a virtual exchange particle in the interaction vertex.
≺=𐑿: The W boson carries a definite electric charge (±1) and weak isospin, mediating interactions with a signed directionality where W⁺ emits positive charge/lepton number and W⁻ absorbs it, creating a distinct donor/acceptor polarity at each vertex.
⋈=𐑐: The W boson mediates weak interactions with a precisely determined coupling strength and vertex structure dictated by gauge symmetry, ensuring near-certain flavor-changing transitions at the interaction vertex when kinematically allowed.
⊤=𐑤: The W boson's weak interactions proceed at measurable rates governed by the Fermi constant, with lifetimes (e.g., muon decay ~2.2 μs) indicating a moderate energy barrier accessible under thermal and quantum perturbations without being kinetically frozen.
∈=𐑲: The W boson mediates weak interactions at a single spacetime vertex with a propagator range limited by its ~80 GeV mass to ~10⁻¹⁸ m, influencing only the immediate fermion pair without propagating correlations to neighboring particles.
∋=𐑜: The W boson couples to any fermion-antifermion pair from the set of weak isospin doublets (e.g., u-d, c-s, e-νₑ, μ-νₘ, τ-νₜ) with universal gauge strength, allowing any valid flavor-changing partner to participate at the vertex.
